results.question: Does the accumulating Vanguard All-World ETF hold every stock in the index or a sample?
results.answer:
The accumulating Vanguard FTSE All-World UCITS ETF (USD) (IE00BK5BQT80) holds a **representative sample** of the index's constituent securities, not every stock. It buys the securities physically. The KID says the fund aims to "track the performance of the Index by investing through physical acquisition in a representative sample of Index constituent securities" [IE00BK5BQT80 KID p.1]. The factsheet gives the same policy and lists the investment method as "Physical" [IE00BK5BQT80 factsheet p.1].

The documents don't give the number of holdings or the sampling method in detail. The KID also notes the fund "typically will not match the performance of the targeted Index exactly" and points to the prospectus for the expected tracking error [IE00BK5BQT80 KID p.1].

results.question: Why might the costs shown in the KID differ from the TER on the factsheet?
results.answer:
The KID and the factsheet measure different things, so the figures can differ even for the same fund.

- **The KID splits costs into more lines.** Its "management fees and other administrative or operating costs" line is an estimate based on the last year's actual costs, and it is shown separately from "transaction costs," which are the costs of buying and selling the fund's underlying investments. The factsheet's TER or ongoing charges figure is a single expense ratio. In the sample I checked, the transaction cost line was the source of any gap. For example, the Vanguard FTSE All-World UCITS ETF (USD) Accumulating (IE00BK5BQT80) has an OCF of 0.14% on its factsheet [IE00BK5BQT80 factsheet p.1]. Its KID shows 0.14% for management and operating costs, plus 0.02% for transaction costs, for a total of 0.16% [IE00BK5BQT80 KID p.3]. The 0.02% is an estimate that varies with how much the fund trades.

- **Where the KID and factsheet match.** The iShares Core S&P 500 UCITS ETF (IE00B5BMR087) has a factsheet TER of 0.07% [IE00B5BMR087 factsheet p.1]. Its KID shows 0.07% for management and operating costs and 0.00% for transaction costs [IE00B5BMR087 KID p.3].

- **Where they can diverge.** The iShares Core MSCI World UCITS ETF (IE00B4L5Y983) shows 0.20% for management and operating costs in its KID, with 0.00% transaction costs [IE00B4L5Y983 KID p.3]. I did not check its factsheet, so I can't say whether its TER matches that figure.

- **Other KID-only items.** The KID also includes entry and exit costs, which are zero for these funds, and performance fees, which are also zero for these funds. The KID's "costs over time" tables then apply these percentages to an example investment amount, so they show money amounts as well as percentages. Those amounts are illustrations, not a fee the fund charges.

- **Timing.** The KID is a dated, regulatory document. The factsheet is a monthly snapshot. Each uses its own calculation basis, so the two can differ slightly even when the underlying costs have not changed.
